Seeded sign-in
Each seeded member exchanges their email and password at `POST /api/auth/login` for a bearer token and their user, `GET /api/auth/me` describes them, and `POST /api/auth/logout` revokes the token.

Refused sign-in and missing sessions
A wrong password and an unknown email both answer `401` with the same copy until the DP-39 throttle applies, and repeated failures for one address are throttled with `429`, while every JSON route except health and login answers `401` without a valid token, as stated in API.

Sign-in in the browser
A signed-out page request lands on the sign-in page with its `next` path and returns there after sign-in, the session survives a reload, `Sign out` ends it, and a throttled sign-in shows its message and keeps the email.

Seeded fleet
The ten seeded trucks are listed in id order with their depot, state and open request, the list narrows by state, and `/fleet` shows the fleet summary line.

Seeded requests and stops
The four seeded requests are stored once each with the statuses, trucks, decisions, four ordered stops and activity given in Seed data.

Dispatch board
The board lists submitted requests oldest first with a summary of the count waiting, the trucks still needed and the trucks available, computed from stored rows.

Request validation
A request with a bad tour name, type, truck count, stop, note, draft id or out-of-order stop dates is refused with `422` and nothing is stored.

Stored submission
A valid request is stored `submitted` with the next consecutive `LR-` id, its four stops and one `submitted` activity entry reading its requested truck count, and fields such as status or requester sent in the body are ignored.

New request in the browser
A tour manager walks the three New request steps, lands on the `Request submitted` page and follows `View request` to the stored request.

Step rules in the browser
`Back` keeps what was typed, a refused step keeps its input and shows the reason, a later step opened early returns to the earliest unfinished step, and `Cancel` on a typed step asks to discard.

Request list API
`GET /api/requests` lists requests newest first in pages of at most 100 with an `X-Next-Cursor` header while more follow, narrows by `status` and `q`, and refuses a bad `status`, `limit` or `cursor` with `400`.

Search, filter and paging in the page
The `Search requests` field and the `Status` select narrow the list in place and are reflected in the address, an empty search offers `Clear search`, and `Show more requests` appends the next page under the same filters.

Request visibility
A tour manager lists and reads only their own requests, with `404` for anyone else's by id, while dispatchers and admins read every request.

Not-found pages
A hidden or missing request and any unknown address show their not-found copy with a real not-found status and a way back to requests.

Request page
A request page shows its four numbered stop cards, its trucks with the count line and its activity timeline, and a timeline that fails to load offers `Try again`.

Truck assignment
A dispatcher assigns one available truck at a time to a submitted request, which marks the truck assigned in storage and writes `truck_assigned` activity.

Assignment conflicts
A busy or parked truck and a truck beyond the requested count are refused with `409` and their copy, an unknown truck with `422`, and nothing changes.

Truck release
Releasing a truck from a submitted request makes it available again with `truck_released` activity, and releasing an existing truck not on a submitted request answers `404`, as qualified in Business rules.

Confirmation
Confirming a fully assigned request with a note records the decider, the time and the note, while confirming with too few trucks answers `409`.

Decline and decided once
Declining releases every truck and records the note, a bad decision is refused with `422`, and any assignment, release or decision on a decided request answers `409`.

One winner
Two simultaneous assignments of one truck, or two simultaneous decisions on one request, produce exactly one success and one `409`.

Dispatch in the browser
A dispatcher reads the board summary, opens a request, assigns two trucks from `Assign truck`, writes a note, confirms and lands on `Decision recorded`.

Dispatch panel feedback
Assigning or releasing shows its notice and updates the trucks, count line and timeline in place, while an early confirm or a decline without a note shows its reason and leaves the request submitted.

Tour managers kept out of dispatch
A tour manager is refused the board, the fleet, every assignment and every decision with `403` at the API, a role sent in a body grants nothing, and the pages show no dispatch controls.

Fleet maintenance
Only an admin moves an available truck into maintenance and back, and a truck on a request is refused with `409`.

Maintenance in the browser
An admin chooses `Start maintenance` on `TR-108` on the fleet page and sees `Truck updated` with the truck in maintenance and the fleet summary line updated.

Closed membership
Members are listed and changed by admins only, there is no sign-up endpoint or page, and no quote, upload or password reset surface exists.

Role changes
An admin's role change is stored, only the role is read from the body, and demoting the only admin is refused with `409`.

Role change in the browser
An admin makes Milo Manager a dispatcher on the members page and sees `Role saved`.

Accessibility
The sign-in page and the signed-in pages meet WCAG 2.2 AA with no serious or critical violation, keyboard focus reaches the navigation with a visible ring, and the current navigation item is marked.

Phone width
At a 360 pixel viewport no page scrolls sideways and the sidebar folds behind a `Menu` button.

Motion
Button labels roll on hover, page headline lines rise one after another, the slogan rail drifts on its named loop and a ring spinner turns while the timeline loads, as described in Motion and effects.

Reduced motion
Under the system reduced-motion preference, or with the remembered `Reduce motion` switch on, no motion runs and every final state shows at once.

No outside hosts
The pages contact no host other than the app's own origin.

Health and production serving
`GET /api/health` answers `{"status": "ok"}` without a session from a production server once the database is ready, and the sign-in page arrives server-rendered.

Stage-dark look
The desk follows the near-black canvas, condensed display type, status chips, line icons, violet-blue actions and closing band described in Visual design.

Desk layouts
The request page, the three steps, the submission confirmation and the phone cards follow the arrangement described in Screens and layout.

Source integrity
The database address comes from the environment, roles are read from stored members, every multi-row write lands whole or not at all, and every record lives in PostgreSQL.

Sign-in throttle
After five failed sign-ins for one address within the lockout window, every further sign-in for that address answers `429` with `Retry-After`, counted in PostgreSQL the same way for known and unknown emails, as qualified in Business rules.

One count of the fleet
Each request's trucks and count, the board's trucks needed and available, each truck's request and the fleet summary agree with the stored assignment rows after any sequence of writes.

Stable request pages
Paging the request list with its cursor never repeats or skips a request while new requests arrive, and filters and ownership apply to every page.

Honest panel after a stale page
A refused panel action shows the server's message in the status region and redraws the trucks, count line, `Assign truck` options and status chip from stored rows.

Declined requests hold no trucks
After a decline its trucks are gone from the request on every surface and free at once, and a racing assignment or release never leaves a truck on a declined request or a request confirmed short.

One request per draft
A repeated `draft_id` from the same member returns the stored request with `200`, two simultaneous posts of one draft store exactly one request, and simultaneous distinct posts get consecutive ids without errors.

Ownership on every derived surface
A tour manager's search, paging, activity, confirmation pages and fragment addresses never reveal another manager's request and answer exactly as a missing id does.

Maintenance against assignment
Starting or ending maintenance on a truck while it is being assigned yields exactly one winner and a consistent fleet row.

Role changes apply at once and keep one admin
A role change applies on the member's very next request, including tokens and pages issued before it, and two admins demoting each other at once leave exactly one admin.
`/app/run.json` exists with `"_schema": "run-manifest-v1"` and string `install`, `build` and `serve` commands, and nothing else is needed to start the app.
`/app/USER_README.md` lists every seeded account email beside the password `deku-demo-pw-2026`.

Shipped packages, meaning the production dependency tree reported by `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`, include no second datastore, cache, queue or embedded database package, and no database file sits in the app tree.
`/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` names every shipped package (the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`) with its version and licence.
Every shipped package (the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`) is under MIT, ISC, 0BSD, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause or Apache-2.0.
The provided service configuration is left as given, and the app reaches PostgreSQL only through `DATABASE_URL`.
